intro: Good experiments follow three principles: control (hold other variables constant, often with a control or placebo group), randomization (randomly assign subjects to treatments to balance unknown variables), and replication (enough subjects, and repeating the study). Blinding hides treatment identity: single-blind hides it from subjects, double-blind from both subjects and those measuring the response. A matched-pairs design compares two treatments within pairs (or the same subject) to reduce variability. The placebo effect is a response to receiving any treatment.

items.prompt: Name the three principles of experimental design.

steps: Second, randomize the assignment of subjects to treatments.
Third, replicate: use enough subjects and repeat.
These three are control, randomization, and replication.

items.prompt: In a drug trial, neither the patients nor the doctors measuring outcomes know who got the drug. What is this called?

steps: Hiding the treatment from the subjects is one layer of blinding.
Hiding it from those measuring the response is a second layer.
Both hidden means it is double-blind.

items.prompt: Each subject tries both a new shoe and an old shoe (one per foot), and times are compared. Name the design.

steps: Both treatments are applied within the same subject (paired).
Differences are compared within each pair.
